However, the candidate completely missed the acceptance criterion requiring the hook's signature or type to make the summed nature unambiguous: it left the `OrchestratorHooks.afterModelResponse` parameter as `usage?: UsageMetadata` (instead of renaming it to `totalUsage` as the reference did in `chatOrchestrator.ts`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md`) and even kept the misleading `lastUsage` local variable name. Additionally, when updating `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`, the candidate edited the bullet in place under the `## Measured semantics — out of scope` section—whose introductory text states that the listed properties are not changed—rather than moving the behavior into the main specification section. Finally, the candidate placed the helper and tests in `orchestratorHelpers.ts` and a new `usageReporting.acceptance.test.ts` file rather than directly in `chatOrchestrator.ts` and `chatOrchestrator.test.ts`.
